subject.title: fix(cli): reject malformed attach ttl values

question: Should explicit `openclaw attach --ttl` values be limited to positive base-10 integer milliseconds even though current releases accept exponent, hexadecimal, and fractional syntax?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but tightening a public CLI flag can break existing scripts and requires maintainer acceptance of that compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Adopt strict integer TTLs
options.body: Treat non-decimal and fractional forms as unsupported, clarify the CLI contract, and merge after real-command proof is added.

options.title: Preserve broader numeric syntax
options.body: Keep the existing accepted grammar or define a different supported grammar before changing validation.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict integer TTLs
recommendation.body: Treat non-decimal and fractional forms as unsupported, clarify the CLI contract, and merge after real-command proof is added.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature history connects this person to the attach CLI and Gateway grant implementation affected by the compatibility choice.
